classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal-length marks, equilateral and isosceles triangles, and supplementary angles to prove a right angle.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with M on straight side CA and segment MB. Double ticks mark CM, MA, MB and AB. No right-angle marker is supplied.
spec.mathematics: CM=MA=MB=AB; C, M and A are collinear. Coordinates satisfy all marked equalities.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible; the right angle at B is not marked.

answer.worked:
$\triangle ABM$ is equilateral, so $\angle AMB=\angle ABM=60^{\circ}$.

$A$, $M$ and $C$ lie on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BMC&=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\angle BMC&=120^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
$MB=MC$, so $\triangle MBC$ is isosceles:
$$\begin{align*}\angle MBC&=\frac{180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle MBC&=30^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=\angle ABM+\angle MBC\\\angle ABC&=60^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\\angle ABC&=90^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
